questions.question: He is attentive ________ his duty.
questions.explanation: 'Attentive to' is the standard preposition used with duty or work.

questions.question: When I finished my work, I asked ________ teacher to check it.
questions.explanation: Possessive determiner 'my' corresponds to the subject 'I'.

questions.question: Those are probably the ________ furniture in the showroom.
questions.explanation: 'Fanciest' is the correct superlative spelling of 'fancy'.

questions.question: They made her ________ a new contract.
questions.explanation: 'Make + object' takes the bare infinitive ('sign') without 'to'.

questions.question: Catching the earlier train will give us the ________ to do some shopping.
questions.explanation: 'Chance' fits the context of an opportunity to do shopping.

questions.question: Reshma bought what she wanted, ________?
questions.explanation: Positive past simple statement 'bought' takes a negative past question tag 'didn't she'.

questions.question: He introduced me ________ his relatives.
questions.explanation: 'Introduce someone to someone' uses the preposition 'to'.

questions.question: She met her mother. She was glad.
options: She was glad to meet her mother.
She met her mother and was gland.
She was glad and met her mother.
She and her mother were glad.
questions.explanation: 'She was glad to meet her mother.' clearly and naturally combines both sentences.

questions.question: He told me, "Are you hungry?"
options: He was asking me if I am hungry.
He asked me if I was hungry.
He said to me if I was hungry.
He questioned me about my hunger.
questions.explanation: Yes/no question 'Are you hungry?' shifts to 'if I was hungry' in indirect speech.

questions.question: You ________ give up smoking.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong advice or obligation to quit smoking.

questions.question: Success depends ________ hard labour.
questions.explanation: The verb 'depend' is followed by the preposition 'on'.

questions.question: He ________ a thief last night.
questions.explanation: 'Last night' indicates past simple, so 'saw' is correct.

questions.question: The synonym of 'show' is:
questions.explanation: 'Exhibit' means to display or show.

questions.question: By whom was the bird killed?
questions.explanation: 'Was killed' is simple past passive, corresponding to active 'Who killed the bird?'

questions.question: The antonym of 'Natural' is:
questions.explanation: 'Artificial' is the opposite of 'natural'.

questions.question: Our path is beset ________ difficulties.
questions.explanation: 'Beset with' is the standard collocation meaning troubled or surrounded by difficulties.

questions.question: I ________ you to read the book carefully.
questions.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb form (whereas 'advice' is the noun).

questions.question: ________ I could sing, I would have sung.
questions.explanation: 'If' introduces the conditional clause.

questions.question: I would have bought a new car for her, but it ________ too expensive.
questions.explanation: Singular 'it' in past tense takes 'was'.

questions.question: The aeroplane flies faster than birds. (Choose the correct negative form)
options: The aeroplane does not fly faster than birds.
The aeroplane flies not fly faster than birds.
The aeroplane many not fly faster than birds.
The aeroplane cannot fly faster than birds.
questions.explanation: Simple present 'flies' negates with 'does not fly'.

questions.question: He was brought ________ by his aunt after his mother's death.
questions.explanation: 'Bring up' / 'brought up' means to raise or care for a child.

questions.question: Choose the incorrect sentence:
options: We saw deers in the zoo.
questions.explanation: 'Deer' is already plural in form ('deers' is incorrect).

questions.question: Keep quiet, we ________ to the radio.
questions.explanation: 'Keep quiet' indicates an ongoing action right now: 'are listening'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: 'Further' is the correct spelling.

questions.question: This nonsense will not be tolerated by me. (Choose the active voice)
options: Will I never tolerate this nonsense?
I will not tolerate this nonsense.
I had not tolerated this nonsense.
Nonsense will not be tolerated by I.
questions.explanation: Future passive 'will not be tolerated by me' converts to 'I will not tolerate this nonsense.'

questions.question: We ________ keep our country free from racial prejudices.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses moral duty or obligation.

questions.question: Have you ________ him?
questions.explanation: 'Have + V3' requires the past participle 'seen'.

questions.question: He told the boy not to sit there. (Choose the direct speech)
options: "Doesn't sit there," he said to the boy.
"Didn't sit there," he said to the boy.
"Didn't sit here," he said to the boy.
"Don't sit here," he said to the boy.
questions.explanation: Negative imperative 'not to sit there' corresponds to direct command '"Don't sit here."'

questions.question: Do you ________ your first teacher?
questions.explanation: After auxiliary 'Do', the base verb 'remember' is used.

questions.question: After his death, the seat remained vacant. ('vacant' means)
questions.explanation: 'Vacant' means empty or unoccupied.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: She will return to India tomorrow.
She has already returned to India tomorrow.
She had returned to India tomorrow for health.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' requires future tense 'will return'.

questions.question: ________ is bad for health.
questions.explanation: Gerund 'Smoking' acts as the subject of the sentence.

questions.question: Holi is ________ important festival.
questions.explanation: 'Important' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: 'Actual' is the correct spelling.

questions.question: I will never forget this experience. (Choose the passive voice)
options: This experience cannot be forgotten by me.
This experience would never be forgotten by me.
This experience will never been be forgotten by me.
This experience will never be forgotten by me.
questions.explanation: Active 'will never forget' becomes passive 'will never be forgotten' (Note: in the PDF option (c) has a typo 'been be', while standard passive is 'will never be forgotten').

questions.question: One who dies for a noble cause is a:
questions.explanation: A person who dies for a noble cause or country is called a martyr.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Which came first, chicken or egg?
Which came first, a chicken or the eggs?
Which came first, the chicken or the eggs?
Which came first, an chicken or an eggs?
questions.explanation: 'Which came first, the chicken or the eggs?' uses proper articles/plurals.

questions.question: The flat caught fire. All the things were burnt.
options: The flat caught fire and all the things was burnt.
The flat having caught fire, all the things were burnt.
All the things was burnt when the flat caught fire.
As all things burnt, the flat caught fire.
questions.explanation: Perfect participle phrase 'The flat having caught fire,' smoothly joins the cause and result.

questions.question: He is a man of ________.
questions.explanation: 'A man of letters' means a scholar or writer.

questions.question: We met a lot of people ________ our holidays.
questions.explanation: 'During' is used for a period of time such as holidays.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: 'Acquaintance' is the correct spelling.

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym of 'Change':
questions.explanation: 'Alter' means to change or modify.

questions.question: He has ________ the prize.
questions.explanation: 'Has + V3' requires the past participle 'won'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: You can vote only when you are eighteen.
You can vote till you are eighteen.
You vote as you are eighteen.
questions.explanation: 'You can vote only when you are eighteen.' states the age condition accurately.

questions.question: ________ he went for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'As usual' fits a routine action like going for a walk.

questions.question: I cannot give you money, ________ I have none.
questions.explanation: 'For' here acts as a conjunction meaning 'because'.

questions.question: Rules ________ be observed at all costs.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses obligation or duty regarding rules.

questions.question: She has learned her lessons. (Choose the passive voice)
options: Her lessons has learned by her.
Her lessons has been learned by her.
Her lessons have been learned by her.
questions.explanation: Plural subject 'Her lessons' takes 'have been learned'.

questions.question: Is there ________ money in your pocket?
questions.explanation: 'Any' is commonly used in interrogative sentences.

questions.question: Choose the odd one:
questions.explanation: Fox, leopard, and lion are mammals/animals, whereas pigeon is a bird.

questions.question: Bring ________ inkpot for me.
questions.explanation: 'Inkpot' starts with a vowel sound, requiring 'an'.

questions.question: He lives in a two-________ house.
questions.explanation: 'Two-storeyed house' is the standard term for a house with two floors.

questions.question: John or Mary ________ gone to Kolkata.
questions.explanation: Singular subjects joined by 'or' take singular 'has gone'.

questions.question: Pravin rode straight ________ the arena.
questions.explanation: 'Into' indicates movement from outside to inside an enclosed space like an arena.

questions.question: Give one word substitution for: 'A person who presents a radio/television programme'
questions.explanation: A host/presenter of a TV or radio show is called an anchor.

questions.question: His honesty and faithfulness ________ unquestionable.
questions.explanation: Two qualities joined by 'and' form a plural subject, taking 'are'.

questions.question: He is happy of being here. (Choose the correct antonym of 'happy')
questions.explanation: 'Sad' is the antonym of 'happy'.

questions.question: Ram said to Shyam, "What are you reading?"
options: Ram asked Shyam what he was reading.
Ram told Shyam what he is reading.
Ram is asking Shyam about his reading book.
Ram said to Shyam about his reading book.
questions.explanation: Past 'said to' + 'What are you reading?' becomes 'asked Shyam what he was reading.'

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: 'Exhibition' is the correct spelling.

questions.question: You need to buy ________ dictionary.
questions.explanation: 'Dictionary' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.question: Goldsmith and Sheridan made contributions to the ________.
questions.explanation: Oliver Goldsmith and Richard Brinsley Sheridan were notable 18th-century playwrights for the English stage.

questions.question: Wole Soyinka is a ________ poet.
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka is a celebrated Nigerian playwright and poet.

questions.question: The Old English Period is characterized by ________.
questions.explanation: Old English was heavily inflected.

questions.question: A major linguistic change in English is ________.
questions.explanation: The Great Vowel Shift was a major phonetic/linguistic change in the history of English.

questions.question: 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast' talks about the ________ of human life.
questions.explanation: W.H. Auden's poem reflects on human mortality, aging, and frustrations in modern life.

questions.question: 'Thou watchest the last oozings hours by hours.' is from:
questions.explanation: This line appears in John Keats's 'Ode to Autumn' ('To Autumn').

questions.question: "And when I crumble, who will remember." Who is 'I' in the line?
questions.explanation: In Walter de la Mare's 'An Epitaph', the speaker ('I') is the poet reflecting on mortality.

questions.question: 'In hearts at peace, under an English heaven' is from:
questions.explanation: This line is from Rupert Brooke's 'The Soldier'.

questions.question: 'Some of the immediate and brilliant results of modern inventions are too maddening to resist' is from:
questions.explanation: This sentence is from Mahatma Gandhi's 'Indian Civilization and Culture'.

questions.question: India was a part of the background of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes', Pearl S. Buck says India was part of her background.

questions.question: Emancipation Proclamation gave the Negro ________.
questions.explanation: The Emancipation Proclamation brought freedom from slavery to Black Americans/Negroes.

questions.question: Bertrand Russell was also a ________.
questions.explanation: Bertrand Russell was a philosopher and mathematician.

questions.question: "Civilization is that mode of conduct which points out to man the path of duty" is from:
questions.explanation: This famous definition is from Mahatma Gandhi's 'Indian Civilization and Culture'.

questions.question: "The people have chosen to make me the head of this family for a certain time." Who says this?
questions.explanation: Dr. Zakir Hussain says this in his inaugural address 'Bharat is My Home'.

questions.question: Who travelled free with Nanukaka?
questions.explanation: In 'A Pinch of Snuff', a kitten travelled in the basket with Nanukaka.

questions.question: Martin Luther King, Jr. asks the black to continue working with ________.
questions.explanation: In 'I Have a Dream', Martin Luther King Jr. urges working with faith.

questions.question: English language is ________ than Sanskrit and Persian.
questions.explanation: English is younger than classical languages like Sanskrit and Persian.

questions.question: The word 'drama' comes from a ________ word.
questions.explanation: 'Drama' originates from a Greek word.

questions.question: Who wrote, "The Scholar Gypsy"?
questions.explanation: 'The Scholar-Gipsy' is written by Matthew Arnold.

questions.question: ________ is called the father of modern novel.
questions.explanation: Henry Fielding is known as the father of the modern novel.

questions.question: The Gujarati equivalent for civilization means ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Indian Civilization and Culture', Gandhi notes the Gujarati equivalent means 'good conduct'.

questions.question: Nanukaka was coming to Delhi to ________.
questions.explanation: In 'A Pinch of Snuff', Nanukaka came to Delhi to see a minister.

questions.question: ________ works include 'Leaves of Grass' and 'Drum Taps.'
questions.explanation: 'Leaves of Grass' and 'Drum-Taps' are works by Walt Whitman.

questions.question: Who 'run scolding for their food' in 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast'?
questions.explanation: In Auden's poem, 'Trolls run scolding for their food.'

questions.question: When we speak of 'the freedom of the press', we usually mean freedom in a ________ sense.
questions.explanation: In 'How Free is the Press?', Dorothy L. Sayers discusses freedom of the press primarily in a technical sense.

questions.question: 'A Marriage Proposal' is a ________.
questions.explanation: Anton Chekhov's 'A Marriage Proposal' is a farce/comedy.

questions.question: Donne studied law and read ________.
questions.explanation: John Donne studied law and read theology.

questions.question: 'I celebrate myself, and sing myself, ________' is from:
options: Now the Leaves are Falling Fast
questions.explanation: This is the opening line of Walt Whitman's 'Song of Myself'.

questions.question: In which poem does the poet express his sad feeling for a beautiful lady?
questions.explanation: In 'An Epitaph', Walter de la Mare grieves for a most beautiful lady.

questions.question: ________ is remembered as a war poet.
questions.explanation: Rupert Brooke is remembered as a World War I poet.

questions.question: Who finds Macavity lazy and half asleep?
questions.explanation: In T.S. Eliot's 'Macavity: The Mystery Cat', Macavity appears lazy and half asleep.

questions.question: D. H. Lawrence exalts the values of primitive life in ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Snake', D.H. Lawrence appreciates the natural/primitive dignity of the snake over modern urban conditioning.

questions.question: 'Macavity: The Mystery Cat' has been taken from:
options: Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
questions.explanation: The poem is from T.S. Eliot's 'Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats'.

questions.question: 'Crossing of Rivers' is an important volume of verse written by:
questions.explanation: 'Crossing of Rivers' is a poetry collection by Keki N. Daruwala.

questions.question: 'He lifted his head from his drinking' is from:
questions.explanation: This line is from D.H. Lawrence's 'Snake'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Huckleberry Finn'?
questions.explanation: 'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn' is a famous novel by Mark Twain.

questions.question: Who wrote the piece 'Why I am Not a Christian'?
questions.explanation: 'Why I Am Not a Christian' is an essay by Bertrand Russell.

questions.question: Seibei was passionately interested in ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Artist', Seibei was passionately interested in gourds.

questions.question: All technological changes cause ________ problems.
questions.explanation: In 'A Child is Born', Germaine Greer notes technological changes cause social problems.

questions.question: Benjy understood about the business of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Earth', Benjy understood everything about keeping hens.

questions.question: Write an essay on any one of the following in about 150-200 words: (a) Elections (b) Child is the father of Man (c) Impact of Covid 19 on society (d) Importance of sports (e) A Picnic Party
questions.explanation: Subjective essay writing question (150-200 words).

questions.question:
Explain any one of the following:
(a) It is obvious that we know more than animals do, and it is common to consider this one of our advantages.
(b) I called the dhobi, and uncle gave him the coat and took him outside and had a talk with him.
(c) The past is not dead and static, it is alive and dynamic....
(d) "There's absolutely no future for a boy like you."
questions.explanation: (a) 'Ideas that Have Helped Mankind'. (b) 'A Pinch of Snuff'. (c) 'Bharat is My Home'. (d) 'The Artist'.

questions.question:
Explain any one of the following:
(a) And what I assume you shall assume, for every atom belonging to me as good belongs to you.
(b) Cold, impossible, ahead Lifts the mountain's lovely head Whose white waterfall could bless Travellers in their last distress.
(c) If I should die, think only this of me: That there's some corner in a foreign field That is forever England.
(d) There is a house now far away where once I received love.
questions.explanation: (a) 'Song of Myself'. (b) 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast'. (c) 'The Soldier'. (d) 'My Grandmother's House'.

questions.question: Write a letter to your friend asking him to visit your village in the winter vacation. OR Write a letter to your Headmaster, asking him to let you use the reading room of the library after the school is over.
questions.explanation: Subjective letter writing question.

questions.question:
Answer any five of the following in about 40-50 words:
(a) Was the Snake conscious of the poet's presence?
(b) How are autumn and summer related to spring?
(c) In what sense does the fire forget its dead?
(d) How did Seibei's father react to the teacher's complaint?
(e) How does Mahatma Gandhi want his countrymen to deal with modern civilization?
(f) What is the reward of pregnancy for a young Sylheti woman?
(g) What was the role of fire in our development?
(h) When did the Great Vowel Shift take place?
(i) What was the impact of the Norman Conquest on the vocabulary of English?
(j) Write a note on English as a Global language.
questions.explanation: Short answer questions (40-50 words each, any 5).

questions.question: Write a summary of any one of the following poems in about 100-120 words: (i) An Epitaph (ii) Ode to Autumn (iii) Song of Myself
questions.explanation: Subjective poetry summary question (100-120 words).

questions.question: Write a summary of any one of the following prose-pieces in about 100-120 words: (i) Bharat is My Home (ii) A Pinch of Snuff (iii) The Earth
questions.explanation: Subjective prose summary question (100-120 words).

questions.question: Write a note on Indian English. OR What are the difficulties faced by an Indian student in learning English? OR Briefly discuss the difference between a short story and a novel.
questions.explanation: Subjective note/discussion question on Story of English.

questions.question: Match the poet 'Kamala Das' with the appropriate work:

questions.question:
Translate any five into English:
(i) तुम कहाँ जा रहे हो?
(ii) सुमिता गा चुकी है।
(iii) हमें बड़ों का आदर करना चाहिए।
(iv) मेरी कक्षा में सौ विद्यार्थी हैं।
(v) वह घर पहुँच चुका होगा।
(vi) शाम में तुम्हें बाजार जाना होगा।
(vii) मुझे वह किताब चाहिए।
(viii) गुरु-शिष्य का संबंध पवित्र होता है।
questions.explanation: (i) Where are you going? (ii) Sumita has sung. (iii) We should respect our elders. (iv) There are a hundred students in my class. (v) He/She will have reached home. (vi) You will have to go to the market in the evening. (vii) I want/need that book. (viii) The guru-disciple relationship is sacred.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
Trees protect the environment and provide oxygen. They prevent soil erosion. Excessive cutting of trees have aggravated many ecological problems. Despite many awareness campaigns, people have not put an end to the practice of cutting trees. We do not realise that by disturbing the ecological balance in nature, we are ourselves paving the way for breakdown of the life-support system.
Questions: (a) What do trees do? (b) What has aggravated the ecological problems? (c) Which practice have we still not stopped? (d) Make sentences with: Environment, Protect.
OR Write a precis of the passage on health and give a suitable title.
questions.explanation: Comprehension answers: (a) Protect environment, give oxygen, prevent soil erosion. (b) Excessive cutting of trees. (c) Cutting down trees. Precis title: The Value of Good Health.
